chunks: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When innovations appear in my community, the scholar should manifest his knowledge. So whoever does not do so, upon him be the curse of God.'

key_terms.الْبِدَعُ: bid'ah (pl. bida') — blameworthy religious innovations not grounded in Quran or authenticated Sunnah; in classical Shia jurisprudence, bid'ah encompasses any doctrine or practice introduced into religion without valid authority
key_terms.الْعَالِمُ: 'alim (scholar) — one possessing authoritative religious knowledge, with the duty to transmit and defend correct teaching
key_terms.لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ: la'nat Allah — the Curse of God; invoking divine curse (la'nah) is among the strongest condemnations in classical Arabic religious discourse

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about scholars remaining silent when religious innovations appear?
ai.summary: This hadith, attributed to the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) through a mursal chain, places a solemn obligation on Islamic scholars to actively counter religious innovations (bid'ah) by openly teaching correct doctrine. The Prophet's warning reflects the early Islamic concern that scholarly silence in the face of heresy is not merely negligence but a grave sin worthy of divine curse. For the original Shia Muslim audience, who faced the challenge of distinguishing authentic Prophetic and Imamic teachings from later innovations, this narration served as a mandate for religious scholars to remain vigilant and publicly engaged.
